open_points.subject: owner visibility of anonymised projects
open_points.text: The Owner “sees the whole catalogue”, but “an anonymised project is never listed” even though it still exists with an id, archived status and artifact pointers.
open_points.question: How can the owner discover and navigate anonymised projects after they disappear from the only project-list action?
options: Include anonymised stubs in an owner-only catalogue
Provide a separate owner-only anonymised-project list
Narrow “whole catalogue” to projects that have not been anonymised
open_points.default_guess: Include owner-only stubs containing only the values anonymisation keeps.

open_points.subject: external language-model boundary
open_points.text: The text says the agent runs in VM Agent and refers only generically to “any language-model agent” and “the external AI providers”; it does not say whether inference is local or which agent-visible values leave VM Agent for an external system.
open_points.question: Is the model an external system, and what agent inputs and outputs cross that trust boundary?
options: Inference is remote and every agent-visible value may reach the named model provider
Inference is local and no model data leaves VM Agent
Both modes are supported with separately declared boundaries
open_points.default_guess: Treat the model provider as an external processor that receives every value visible to the agent, while never receiving Registry-classified personal_data.

open_points.subject: personal-data guarantee through other trusted services
open_points.text: The Agent actor says it “never receives a value Registry holds as personal_data”, while R0-74 says values that personal-data-cleared services pass to Kernel are “bounded by their own contracts, not here”. Cabinet receives Registry personal_data and can communicate with Kernel.
open_points.question: Is the no-personal-data promise end-to-end across Cabinet and every other service, or only a promise about Registry's direct outputs to Cabinet Kernel?
options: Require every service contract to prevent Registry personal_data from reaching Kernel or the agent
Narrow the promise to Registry's direct Kernel-facing operations
Remove personal_data access from services that can pass values to Kernel
open_points.default_guess: Keep the end-to-end promise and make the Cabinet-to-Kernel prohibition an explicit required external contract.

open_points.subject: customer erasure and fiscal data
open_points.text: “erase a customer's contact data” names only name, phone, e-mail and language as removed, but its output says the Customer “keeps only its identity and the fact that it was erased”; R0-67 likewise calls this the end of the record, while the changed model also stores tax id and legal name.
open_points.question: Does erasing a customer also erase tax id and legal name, or do those fiscal values remain stored in an erased and otherwise unusable Customer?
options: Erase contact and fiscal data, leaving only identity and the erased marker
Erase contact data but retain fiscal data
Provide separate contact-data and fiscal-data erasure actions
open_points.default_guess: Erase both contact and fiscal data so that only identity and the erased marker remain.

open_points.subject: revision coverage for state-changing actions
open_points.text: R0-35 says a Project or Customer revision is moved by “every accepted change” and R0-29 says “Every change” made against an older revision is refused, but only the correction actions mention a next revision or stale-revision failure. Archiving, customer erasure, restriction, relationship changes, room creation and project anonymisation do not say whether they move or require a revision.
open_points.question: Exactly which actions require an expected revision, which aggregate's revision they check, and which revisions they advance?
options: Every mutation of a Project or Customer aggregate checks and advances its revision
Only direct correction actions use revisions
Declare a per-action revision matrix, including rooms, pointers, archive, restriction, relationship state and erasure
open_points.default_guess: Declare a per-action matrix; require revisions for every direct Project or Customer state change and advance the affected aggregate revision.

open_points.subject: owner-interface concurrency outside Project and Customer
open_points.text: The owner interface carries every owner action and says “Every change” against an older revision is refused, but agent-session access, pending requests, import and audit retention have no record revision defined; only session access exposes an unexplained “access version”.
open_points.question: What concurrency token, if any, protects owner changes to session access, pending requests, the one-time import and audit erasure?
options: Use access version for every session mutation and define separate tokens for other mutable resources
Limit the stale-change promise to Project and Customer changes
Give every owner form a resource-specific version or one-time confirmation token
open_points.default_guess: Use access version for session mutations and explicitly limit revision checks elsewhere to versioned resources.

open_points.subject: meaning of session access version
open_points.text: “read the session's access” returns “the access version”, but no action says what creates it, which changes advance it, whether pending-request replacement advances it, or whether owner and Kernel writes must present it.
open_points.question: What observable meaning and concurrency behavior does the session access version have?
options: Advance it on every change to grants, active project or pending request and require it for owner mutations
Advance it only when grants or the active project change
Expose it only as an informational change counter
open_points.default_guess: Advance it on every change to grants, active project or pending request and require it when the owner answers or changes session access.

open_points.subject: audit event coverage
open_points.text: The audit log records “significant changes of state”, followed by a non-exhaustive-looking list, while the changed actions also register sessions, replace and answer access requests, change active projects, add rooms, publish or withdraw pointers, import data, end relationships and erase audit entries. R0-37 gives entries an “outcome”, but R0-58 says the log records changes of state and does not say whether refused attempts are entries.
open_points.question: Which successful and refused primary actions produce audit entries, and which are intentionally excluded?
options: Audit every durable state-changing action and selected security-relevant refusals
Audit only the categories literally enumerated in R0-58
Declare an explicit per-action audit matrix
open_points.default_guess: Declare a per-action matrix covering every durable state change, while logging refusals only where explicitly security-relevant.

open_points.subject: migration of customer identities
open_points.text: R0-50 says import “keeps every identity and link: project ids, customer_refs, room and pointer ids and versions”, but the import action says a v1 customer_ref that is not Registry-minted becomes a newly minted customer_ref and the old value may move to tax id.
open_points.question: Which customer_ref values are preserved, and how are project links rewritten when a legacy customer_ref is replaced?
options: Preserve every source customer_ref
Remint only invalid legacy customer_refs and atomically rewrite all links through a declared mapping
Refuse imports containing non-minted customer_refs
open_points.default_guess: Remint invalid legacy customer_refs and atomically rewrite every imported project link using one recorded mapping.

open_points.subject: renaming imported projects named after people
open_points.text: R0-82 says projects imported under a person's name “are renamed by the owner after the import”, but an archived project “cannot be corrected”; the import action does not refuse or transform such archived projects.
open_points.question: What happens if the selected import contains an archived project whose display name names a person?
options: Require the owner to supply the replacement name during import
Allow this one correction after import
Refuse that project or the whole import
Permit the personal display name to remain because it is protected as personal_data
open_points.default_guess: Require the replacement display name as part of the confirmed import mapping.

open_points.subject: personal values retained in anonymised artifact pointers
open_points.text: An anonymised project always keeps artifact pointers and R0-71 says it “holds no personal value”, but R0-68 says Registry does not inspect pointer values and that a uri, payload_ref or digest breaking the writer rule “is not refused and does reach the agent”.
open_points.question: How can anonymisation guarantee that no personal value remains when retained pointer values are neither inspected nor removed?
options: Require a governance check before anonymisation and make confirmation attest that retained pointers contain no identifying value
Remove or redact pointer values during anonymisation
Narrow the guarantee so anonymisation removes only Registry-classified personal_data and may retain violating free text
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit pre-anonymisation review of retained pointers and refuse anonymisation until the owner confirms the governance check.
